questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively complicated. I would say that planning my own trip to Kazakhstan was a comparable experience, which is probably not what ERASMUS is aiming for.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There is an ERASMUS department that you can contact if you want help registering.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy but pretty expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to pay +900 EUR a month for a room.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: THeir semester is running later than the rest of the world's, meaning I wasn't able to register for courses before mid april. Then there was a 2-3 week period, where they weren't able to tell you if you'd actually be allowed to complete the classes you'd registered for. This was infuriating since it also takes close to a month to get the courses preapproved at UCPH. If I remember correctly, I didn't have my preapproval and learning agreement signed before mid June.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The ERASMUS department

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to get into every class that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you're studying politics, there are enough classes taught in English to never have to study in German contrary to what some believe.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses differed extremely in their level. I think this is because I was doing some courses solely meant for exchange students. Humboldt probably wants every student to pass as rescheduling exams are hard if not impossible, meaning the level in those courses was extremely low. In my class on conflicts and economic development the professor spent 45 minutes explaining a linear progression.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some classes were better than what I have ever experienced at UCPH some were worse.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Conflict and Economic Development
Russia's War against Ukraine
Fundamentals of Political Economy
Organised Interests in Political Economy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The two political economy classes were great.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent is more expensive, food is cheaper. However I was living in a house with student apartments, where quite a few wealthy students/young professionals lived, which meant that I ended up spending a lot of money hanging out with them. The exchange trip probably could have been done cheaper.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take the bus or train to other German cities such as Dresden.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: As a Dane it is very easy to fit into German culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I never got acquainted with any.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The amount of mentally ill homeless people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Stalin Allee

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be conscious of where you choose to live, because it is hard to find friends through university
Overestimate your budgetting, it is more expensive than you might think.
If you have the option live close to the city center as you otherwise might spend an hour each way sitting in a train.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take the non ERASMUS classes if possible. The master courses are often taught in English but are mostly German students. This means that the level is way higher.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to use Berlin as a base for roadtripping Germany and the surrounding countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having openly communist professors.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
